preconditions.description: Attacker must hold Touch tokens to set approvals
Contract must be in unrestricted mode (unrestricted == true)

violation_target.exploit_hint: The approve function requires current allowance to be 0 OR new value to be 0. To exploit the race condition: (1) Attacker sets approval to non-zero value for spender, (2) Attacker attempts to change approval to different non-zero value without first setting to 0, (3) This forces a two-step approval change (approve to 0, then approve to new value), creating a window where spender could potentially front-run and spend tokens. Test by calling approve(spender, X) then approve(spender, Y) where both X and Y are non-zero - the second call should revert, demonstrating the protection mechanism.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The Touch token contract implements ERC-20 approve with race condition protection. The approve function requires that either the current allowance is 0 OR the new value is 0 (require(allowed[msg.sender][_spender] == 0 || _value == 0)). This is actually a protection mechanism, not a vulnerability. The oracle checks that allowed[attacker][spender] != 0, meaning we need to successfully set a non-zero approval. The contract is in unrestricted mode by default (unrestricted = true), so the ifUnrestricted modifier will pass.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Inject Touch tokens to the attacker address using deal() cheatcode. 2. Call approve(spender, non-zero-value) when current allowance is 0. 3. This will succeed and set allowed[attacker][spender] to a non-zero value. 4. The oracle verifies the allowance is non-zero.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Define ITouch interface with approve and allowance functions. 2. In setUp, initialize the touch contract instance and spender address. 3. In testExploit, use deal() to give attacker tokens at the token contract. 4. Call touch.approve(spender, 1000 * 1e18) to set non-zero allowance. 5. Oracle verifies allowed[attacker][spender] != 0.
